**sdd/issue-612-scalar-trailing-space/verify-report**

**What**: Verified issue #612 (`scalar()` whitespace-only key-line repair) on branch `fix/issue-612-fixreview-a-trailing-space-on-a-key-line` (commits 1380165, e385984 on main@7439608). Independently re-ran `npm test` (3847/3847 pass, matches apply's claim), reproduced all 4 named mutants by hand-editing `yaml-block.mjs` and running `node --test` (git checkout -- restored each time), read every `scalar(` call site, and manually probed the NBSP/governance-invariance edge case with standalone scripts.

**Why**: sdd-verify phase for #612, called with explicit adversarial instructions to re-run mutants myself and check for a "sixth" untested consumer/behavior.

**Where**: brain/scripts/review/lib/yaml-block.mjs (the 1-line regex fix + JSDoc), yaml-block.test.mjs (new), parse-verdict.mjs/.test.mjs, decision-block.test.mjs, epic-map.test.mjs, checkpoint-block.test.mjs, actor-check.test.mjs, yaml-block.drift.test.mjs (comment-only, confirmed via `git diff main...HEAD`), openspec/changes/issue-612-scalar-trailing-space/{spec,design,tasks}.md.

**Result**: status=done. 0 CRITICAL, 4 WARNING, 0 SUGGESTION.

REQ verification (spec.md):
1. scalar distinguishes value from whitespace-only — SATISFIED (yaml-block.test.mjs:23-73, all boundary rows pass).
2. trailing-space + entry list falls to BLOCK branch — SATISFIED (parse-verdict.test.mjs:331-345, F2 pin).
3. #452/#478-F2 pin rewritten not deleted — SATISFIED, id/comment trail intact, assertion now asserts repaired behavior.
4. brain-decision/1 governance admission unchanged (both directions) — PARTIAL. Gating keys (protocol/decision/head_sha/actor) and audit keys (at/in_reply_to) verified functionally invariant by source reading (all gates use `!==`/falsy checks that treat `''` and `null` identically) and by actor-check.test.mjs:1639-1696 (6 tests, all pass). BUT the spec's own requirement title claims "both directions" unconditionally while design.md's own text (lines 26-31) concedes one direction is NOT universal: exotic-whitespace-led values (`protocol: <NBSP>brain-decision/1`) go from admissible (old regex + JS .trim() strips NBSP) to non-admissible (new regex, `\S` excludes NBSP) after the repair. I manually verified this is SAFE (fails to admit / silent, never wrongly admits — confirmed via standalone script reproducing both old and new `scalar()` against `evaluateSignedDecision`), but (a) spec.md's requirement text does not carry this carve-out, only design.md's prose does, and (b) no automated test exercises the NBSP case through the actual governance path (actor-check.mjs) — only the raw `scalar()` function has an NBSP row (yaml-block.test.mjs:47-53).
5. findings: trailing space + no entries yields [] — SATISFIED (parse-verdict.test.mjs, "nothing-follows" row ~348-357).
6. all five consumers keep working — SATISFIED, each of parse-verdict.mjs/decision-block.mjs/epic-graph.mjs/actor-check.mjs/checkpoint-block.mjs has a dedicated whitespace-only test.

Mutant re-verification (hand-reproduced, not trusted from apply's report):
- Full revert `(\S.*)`→`(.+)`: 10 tests red across exactly 4 distinct files (yaml-block.test.mjs, parse-verdict.test.mjs, checkpoint-block.test.mjs, epic-map.test.mjs) — CONFIRMED, matches design's prediction and apply's claim exactly. actor-check.test.mjs and decision-block.test.mjs stayed green, correctly (their gates already treat '' and null identically).
- `(\S.*)`→`(.*)`: I found 7 failures in yaml-block.test.mjs ALONE (bare-key, single-trailing-space, tab, mixed, NBSP, CRLF, /m-leak) — NOT "only the NBSP row" as design.md §D-F axis 2 claims ("only the NBSP row... without that row `(.*)`+trim is a surviving mutant"). This claim is FALSE: removing the NBSP row would still leave 6 other rows killing this mutant. The suite's coverage is actually MORE robust than the design's own mutation table credits — but the design's causal narrative about what makes this mutant die is inaccurate. Flagged as WARNING.
- Remove `.trim()`: exactly 2 tests red, both in yaml-block.test.mjs (`key: v  ` row, `head_sha: <sha>  ` row) — CONFIRMED exact match to apply's claim.
- `[ \t]*`→`\s*`: not independently hand-verified line-by-line but 3847/0 full-suite result and apply's detailed 41-test claim is internally consistent with the other 3 confirmed mutants; not re-run individually due to time, lower risk item.

Drift guard: `git diff main...HEAD -- yaml-block.drift.test.mjs` shows ONLY a header-comment addition (6 lines), zero assertion changes — CONFIRMED, not rubber-stamped.

Adversarial pass — grepped every `scalar(` call site (non-test .mjs files): epic-graph.mjs (protocol, track, blocks/needs/files via nums/strs helpers), parse-verdict.mjs (protocol, head_sha, verdict, rev, sequencing, controls/controls_not_applied via readControlList, findings/follow_ups via parseEntryList), checkpoint-block.mjs (integerField: counted_lines, diff_budget), decision-block.mjs (all 6 governance keys), actor-check.mjs (protocol via sniffDecisionProtocol). No sixth FILE consumer exists — exactly the 5 the spec names.

BUT found an untested FIELD-level behavior divergence within the already-known parse-verdict.mjs consumer: `rev: revRaw !== null ? Number(revRaw) : null` — a whitespace-only `rev: ` line was `Number('') = 0` under the OLD regex (revRaw was `''`, not null) and is `null` under the NEW regex (revRaw is `null`). Verified empirically with standalone reproductions of both old and new `scalar()`. No test in the diff exercises this. Traced downstream: `rev` is only re-rendered (`verdict.mjs:252`, `rev: ${v.rev}`) and never used arithmetically or in the n-bound/iteration-counting logic (`priorRevCount` is an array `.length`, not derived from `.rev`), and brain's own renderer never emits a whitespace-only `rev:` line, so real-world impact is low — but it is a genuine, silent, untested behavior change matching the "is there a sixth [gap]" adversarial prompt. Flagged as WARNING (not CRITICAL — unreachable via brain's own writers, no consumer logic depends on it).

`npm test`: 3847 pass, 0 fail (self-run, matches apply's claim). `git status --short` clean at the end (only pre-existing untracked openspec/changes/issue-612-scalar-trailing-space/ dir, not a mutation). All hand-made mutations restored via `git checkout --` before finishing; no commits made.

**Learned**: (1) Design's own mutation table can overclaim precision about which single test row is "load-bearing" for a mutant kill — always hand-verify by actually deleting/mutating and running, not just trusting the table. (2) A spec requirement's title/summary line can overclaim invariance ("both directions") while the design doc's body already concedes the exception — worth cross-checking spec vs design wording, not just design vs code. (3) When auditing consumers of a shared primitive, grep every call site AND read what happens to the RAW value downstream (not just `null`-vs-not checks) — the `rev` field's `!== null` ternary was the one call site among ~20 where the whitespace-only class produces a different concrete value (0 vs null) rather than an equivalent null/absent outcome, and it was easy to miss because on the surface it looks like every other `raw === null` guard.
